objective: Research current open-source kernels, AI runtimes, model ecosystems, and paid-model APIs, then implement a provider-neutral model-action envelope that keeps model output separate from authority.

findings: AIOS provides agent-level scheduling, context switching, memory, tool management, and routing above a traditional OS; it is not a Linux kernel replacement.

vLLM provides PagedAttention, continuous batching, prefix caching, disaggregated prefill/decode/encode, distributed parallelism, structured outputs, tool/reasoning parsers, and broad hardware support above the OS.
Qwen documents application-mediated function calling with JSON-schema tools and thinking/no-thinking controls.
seL4 contributes formally verified capability isolation and controlled communication; FAISAL can adopt narrow formalizable policy invariants without claiming whole-kernel formal verification.
Unikraft contributes specialization and fast-startup library-OS ideas; FAISAL can use measured minimal sandbox profiles without abandoning Linux compatibility.
OpenAI Structured Outputs, Anthropic client tools, Gemini function calling, and Qwen function calling all distinguish model-emitted requests from application-side execution.
NCCL, RCCL, and Level Zero remain hardware-specific execution stacks and are not replaced by a policy envelope.

features: provider-neutral OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, and local-provider identities
independent policy or kernel authority requirement
monotonic request-sequence and nonce replay protection
tamper-evident envelope digest binding at completion

benchmark.scope: local userspace policy fixture, not model inference or paid-provider latency

known_boundary.interpretation: The existing virtualization limitation was reproduced and rejected; it was not suppressed or attributed to M227 model-action code.

comparison.scope: FAISAL provider-neutral action governance versus AIOS, vLLM, open-weight model tool protocols, and paid-model APIs
comparison.faisal_advantage: independent authorization, replay/tamper protection, agent/objective/tenant lineage, registry generation binding, and fail-closed model-output boundary
comparison.ecosystem_advantage: AIOS and agent runtimes provide richer user-space agent behavior; vLLM provides real model serving, KV/memory optimization, batching, distributed execution, and hardware plugins; paid providers provide hosted model quality, tools, and multimodal services
comparison.note: M227 improves the control-plane safety contract. It does not train a model, create consciousness, execute paid APIs, implement inference kernels, or prove human-level learning.

boundary.fast_boot_claim: qualified only for the measured ACPI-off one-vCPU QEMU profile; no universal fast-boot claim
boundary.note: The production release gate remains fail-closed. No external model, hardware, reviewer, production signing ceremony, or production approval was fabricated.
